claims.value: Bodart: side A (French) 18,000 infantry and 6,500 cavalry, total 24,500; side B (Spanish) 9,800 infantry and 1,200 cavalry, total 11,000.
claims.rationale: Available-for-engagement figures under Bodart’s rounded-up convention (shared research-conventions index), unless the entry specifies a surrender population. Not an opening muster; components are not added twice. English rendering of the claim-relevant portion (ours): "side A (French) 18,000 infantry and 6,500 cavalry, total 24,500; side B (Spanish) 9,800 infantry and 1,200 cavalry, total 11,000."

claims.value: Toreno counts side B at 12,000 in Burgos and its vicinity, including 1,200 cavalry.
claims.rationale: The complete preceding paragraph gives the approximately 18,000 army and the third division near Lerma. Local availability differs from full army establishment. English rendering (ours): "Thus only 12,000 were counted in the city and vicinity, 1,200 of them cavalry."

citations.locator: toreno-t2, printed p. 152, Internet Archive leaf 157; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: Así que solo se contaban dentro de la ciudad y cercanías 12,000 hombres, de ellos 1200 de caballería.

claims.value: Napoleon assumed Bessières had 15,000 infantry, 5,000 cavalry and 40 guns before the Burgos advance.
claims.rationale: An explicit superior assumption, not the 10 November engaged return. It is not combined with Lapisse’s separate expected reinforcement. English rendering (ours): "I suppose you have 5,000 cavalry, 15,000 infantry and 40 guns."

citations.locator: napoleon-t18, printed p. 38, Internet Archive leaf 47; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: Je suppose que vous avez 5,000 hommes de cavalerie, 15,000 hommes d’infanterie et 40 pièces de canon.

claims.value: Napoleon told Bessières he would send Soult to take over his corps after Burgos was occupied and give Bessières the cavalry.
claims.rationale: Prospective superior order. Bodart and Toreno’s narrative name Soult at the battle, but exact effective transfer time is unestablished. English rendering (ours): "After you complete your mission by occupying Burgos, I shall send Soult to command your corps and give you the cavalry."

citations.locator: napoleon-t18, printed p. 38, Internet Archive leaf 47; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: Immédiatement après que vous aurez fini la mission que je vous ai donnée, en occupant Burgos, j’enverrai le maréchal Soult pour prendre le commandement de votre corps, et je vous donnerai celui de la cavalerie.

claims.value: Toreno says Henestrosa effectively also commanded in chief, an authority alternative to Bodart’s Belveder label.
claims.rationale: Alternative authority, not automatic exclusive attribution. English rendering (ours): "Henestrosa, who in reality also commanded in chief."

claims.value: Toreno says Mouton’s veteran infantry attacked the wood held by the Spanish right.
claims.rationale: The Spanish cavalry charge within the defence does not by itself recode the whole engagement as both attacking. English rendering (ours): "General Mouton’s veteran infantry boldly attacked the wood held by the Spanish right."

claims.value: Toreno places the Spanish left at the walls of an orchard or garden.
claims.rationale: A named occupied wall qualifies under the brief’s walls code; this is not evidence of a purpose-built rampart or entrenchment. Construction authority is unknown. English rendering (ours): "the left [occupied] the walls of an orchard or garden."

open_questions: Separate nominal army, troops near Burgos and the engaged subset; fix effective Soult/Bessières command timing from orders and reports.
Deferred: the dated original returns and reports identified above, and any deeper source-lineage reconciliation. No additional research cycle follows merely from this gap.

Source dependence: Bodart is a later compilation. Toreno, Foy, Oman, Saint-Cyr and the official Correspondance are interested or retrospective source families, and embedded/reprinted reports are not extra independent witnesses. Agreement does not establish independence.

A.strength_population_and_time: Bodart’s engagement-level available force; no dated opening return. Source-specific alternatives below retain their own moment and population. Alternatives/limits: Napoleon assumed Bessières had 15,000 infantry, 5,000 cavalry and 40 guns before the Burgos advance.
A.command_scope: Printed side-A commander Soult; local/superior authority and transitions remain limited to the additional passages cited below. Napoleon told Bessières he would send Soult to take over his corps after Burgos was occupied and give Bessières the cavalry.
A.army_continuity: Unknown: these passages do not establish a cross-engagement army identity.

B.strength_population_and_time: Bodart’s engagement-level available force; no dated opening return. Civilians, recruits, regular troops and surrender survivors are not interchangeable. Alternatives/limits: Toreno counts side B at 12,000 in Burgos and its vicinity, including 1,200 cavalry.
B.command_scope: Printed side-B commander Belveder; local/superior authority and transitions remain limited to the additional passages cited below. Toreno says Henestrosa effectively also commanded in chief, an authority alternative to Bodart’s Belveder label.
B.army_continuity: Unknown: repeated names and formation labels do not establish continuity.
